NASB.1: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'See, I make you [as] God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron shall be your prophet.
NASB.2: 'You shall speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron shall speak to Pharaoh that he let the sons of Israel go out of his land.
NASB.3: 'But I will harden Pharaoh's heart that I may multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.
NASB.4: 'When Pharaoh does not listen to you, then I will lay My hand on Egypt and bring out My hosts, My people the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt by great judgments.
NASB.5: 'The Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand on Egypt and bring out the sons of Israel from their midst.'
NASB.6: So Moses and Aaron did [it]; as the LORD commanded them, thus they did.
NASB.7: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
NASB.8: Now the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
NASB.9: 'When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Work a miracle,' then you shall say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw [it] down before Pharaoh, [that] it may become a serpent.''
NASB.10: So Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh, and thus they did just as the LORD had commanded; and Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his servants, and it became a serpent.
NASB.11: Then Pharaoh also called for [the] wise men and [the] sorcerers, and they also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same with their secret arts.
NASB.12: For each one threw down his staff and they turned into serpents. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.
NASB.13: Yet Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had said.
NASB.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Pharaoh's heart is stubborn; he refuses to let the people go.
NASB.15: 'Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he is going out to the water, and station yourself to meet him on the bank of the Nile; and you shall take in your hand the staff that was turned into a serpent.
NASB.16: 'You shall say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you, saying, 'Let My people go, that they may serve Me in the wilderness. But behold, you have not listened until now.'
NASB.17: 'Thus says the LORD, 'By this you shall know that I am the LORD: behold, I will strike the water that is in the Nile with the staff that is in my hand, and it will be turned to blood.
NASB.18: 'The fish that are in the Nile will die, and the Nile will become foul, and the Egyptians will find difficulty in drinking water from the Nile.'''
NASB.19: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their streams, and over their pools, and over all their reservoirs of water, that they may become blood; and there will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in [vessels of] wood and in [vessels of] stone.''
NASB.20: So Moses and Aaron did even as the LORD had commanded. And he lifted up the staff and struck the water that [was] in the Nile, in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants, and all the water that [was] in the Nile was turned to blood.
NASB.21: The fish that [were] in the Nile died, and the Nile became foul, so that the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile. And the blood was through all the land of Egypt.
NASB.22: But the magicians of Egypt did the same with their secret arts; and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had said.
NASB.23: Then Pharaoh turned and went into his house with no concern even for this.
NASB.24: So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, for they could not drink of the water of the Nile.
NASB.25: Seven days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.

NKJV.1: So the LORD said to Moses: “See, I have made you as God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.
NKJV.2: You shall speak all that I command you. And Aaron your brother shall tell Pharaoh to send the children of Israel out of his land.
NKJV.3: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.
NKJV.4: But Pharaoh will not heed you, so that I may lay My hand on Egypt and bring My armies and My people, the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
NKJV.5: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand on Egypt and bring out the children of Israel from among them.”
NKJV.6: Then Moses and Aaron did so; just as the LORD commanded them, so they did.
NKJV.7: And Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.
NKJV.8: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
NKJV.9: “When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Show a miracle for yourselves,’ then you shall say to Aaron, ‘Take your rod and cast it before Pharaoh, and let it become a serpent.’ ”
NKJV.10: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and they did so, just as the LORD commanded. And Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
NKJV.11: But Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers; so the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments.
NKJV.12: For every man threw down his rod, and they became serpents. But Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.
NKJV.13: And Pharaoh’s heart grew hard, and he did not heed them, as the LORD had said.
NKJV.14: So the LORD said to Moses: “Pharaoh’s heart is hard; he refuses to let the people go.
NKJV.15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning, when he goes out to the water, and you shall stand by the river’s bank to meet him; and the rod which was turned to a serpent you shall take in your hand.
NKJV.16: And you shall say to him, ‘The LORD God of the Hebrews has sent me to you, saying, “Let My people go, that they may serve Me in the wilderness”; but indeed, until now you would not hear!
NKJV.17: Thus says the LORD: “By this you shall know that I am the LORD. Behold, I will strike the waters which are in the river with the rod that is in my hand, and they shall be turned to blood.
NKJV.18: And the fish that are in the river shall die, the river shall stink, and the Egyptians will loathe to drink the water of the river.” ’ ”
NKJV.19: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your rod and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their streams, over their rivers, over their ponds, and over all their pools of water, that they may become blood. And there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in buckets of wood and pitchers of stone.’ ”
NKJV.20: And Moses and Aaron did so, just as the LORD commanded. So he lifted up the rod and struck the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants. And all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
NKJV.21: The fish that were in the river died, the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river. So there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
NKJV.22: Then the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments; and Pharaoh’s heart grew hard, and he did not heed them, as the LORD had said.
NKJV.23: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house. Neither was his heart moved by this.
NKJV.24: So all the Egyptians dug all around the river for water to drink, because they could not drink the water of the river.
NKJV.25: And seven days passed after the LORD had struck the river.

ESV.23: Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not take even this to heart.
ESV.24: And all the Egyptians dug along the Nile for water to drink, for they could not drink the water of the Nile.
ESV.25: Seven full days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.

CSB17.1: The LORD answered Moses, “See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
CSB17.2: You must say whatever I command you; then Aaron your brother must declare it to Pharaoh so that he will let the Israelites go from his land.
CSB17.3: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart <sup>ⓓ</sup> and multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
CSB17.4: Pharaoh will not listen to you, but I will put my hand into Egypt and bring the military divisions of my people the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by great acts of judgment.
CSB17.5: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD <sup>ⓔ</sup> when I stretch out my hand <sup>ⓕ</sup> against Egypt and bring out the Israelites from among them.”
CSB17.6: So Moses and Aaron did this; they did just as the LORD commanded them.
CSB17.7: Moses was eighty years old <sup>ⓖ</sup> and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.
CSB17.8: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
CSB17.9: “When Pharaoh tells you, ‘Perform a miracle,’ tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh. It will become a serpent.’” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.10: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD had commanded. Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent.
CSB17.11: But then Pharaoh called the wise men and sorcerers — the magicians <sup>ⓘ</sup> of Egypt, and they also did the same thing by their occult practices. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.12: Each one threw down his staff, and it became a serpent. But Aaron’s staff swallowed their staffs.
CSB17.13: However, Pharaoh’s heart was hard, <sup>ⓚ</sup> and he did not listen to them, as the LORD had said.
CSB17.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is hard: He refuses to let the people go.
CSB17.15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. When you see him walking out to the water, stand ready to meet him by the bank of the Nile. Take in your hand the staff that turned into a snake. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.16: Tell him: The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you: Let my people go, so that they may worship <sup>[1]</sup> me in the wilderness, but so far you have not listened.
CSB17.17: This is what the LORD says: Here is how you will know that I am the LORD. Watch. I am about to strike the water in the Nile with the staff in my hand, and it will turn to blood.
CSB17.18: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink water from it.”
CSB17.19: So the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron: Take your staff and stretch out your hand <sup>ⓜ</sup> over the waters of Egypt — over their rivers, canals, ponds, and all their water reservoirs — and they will become blood. There will be blood throughout the land of Egypt, even in wooden and stone containers.”
CSB17.20: Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded; in the sight of Pharaoh and his officials, he raised the staff and struck the water in the Nile, and all the water in the Nile was turned to blood. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.21: The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad the Egyptians could not drink water from it. There was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
CSB17.22: But the magicians of Egypt did the same thing by their occult practices. So Pharaoh’s heart was hard, and he would not listen to them, as the LORD had said.
CSB17.23: Pharaoh turned around, went into his palace, and didn’t take even this to heart.
CSB17.24: All the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink because they could not drink the water from the river.
CSB17.25: Seven days passed after the LORD struck the Nile.

AMP.1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Now hear this: I make you as God to Pharaoh [to declare My will and purpose to him]; and your brother Aaron shall be your prophet.
AMP.2: You shall speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron shall tell Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of his land.
AMP.3: And I will make Pharaoh's heart hard, and multiply My signs and My wonders (miracles) in the land of Egypt.
AMP.4: But Pharaoh will not listen to you, and I shall lay My hand on Egypt and bring out My hosts [like a defensive army, tribe by tribe], My people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great acts of judgment (the plagues).
AMP.5: The Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand on Egypt and bring out the children of Israel from among them."
AMP.6: And Moses and Aaron did so; just as the LORD commanded them, so they did.
AMP.7: Now Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.
AMP.8: Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
AMP.9: "When Pharaoh says to you, 'Work a miracle [to prove your authority],' then you say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh, so that it may become a serpent.'"
AMP.10: So Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh, and did just as the LORD had commanded; Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and his servants, and it became a serpent.
AMP.11: Then Pharaoh called for the wise men [skilled in magic and omens] and the sorcerers [skilled in witchcraft], and they also, these magicians (soothsayer-priests) of Egypt, did the same with their secret arts and enchantments.
AMP.12: For every man threw down his staff and they turned into serpents; but Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.
AMP.13: Yet Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
AMP.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is hard; he refuses to let the people go.
AMP.15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he is going out to the water, and wait for him on the bank of the Nile; and you shall take in your hand the staff that was turned into a serpent.
AMP.16: You shall say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, "Let My people go, so that they may serve Me in the wilderness. But behold, you have not listened until now."
AMP.17: Thus says the LORD, "By this you shall know and recognize and acknowledge that I am the LORD: look, with the staff in my hand I will strike the water in the Nile, and it shall be turned to blood.
AMP.18: The fish in the Nile will die, and the Nile will become foul, and the Egyptians will not be able to drink water from the Nile."'"
AMP.19: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their streams, over their pools, and over all their reservoirs of water, so that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, in containers both of wood and of stone.'"
AMP.20: So Moses and Aaron did as the LORD commanded; Aaron lifted up the staff and struck the waters in the Nile, in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants, and all the water that was in the Nile was turned into blood.
AMP.21: The fish in the Nile died, and the river became foul smelling, and the Egyptians could not drink its water, and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
AMP.22: But the magicians of Egypt did the same by their secret arts and enchantments; so Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
AMP.23: Then Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not take even this [divine sign] to heart.

NLT.1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pay close attention to this. I will make you seem like God to Pharaoh, and your brother, Aaron, will be your prophet.
NLT.2: Tell Aaron everything I command you, and Aaron must command Pharaoh to let the people of Israel leave his country.
NLT.3: But I will make Pharaoh’s heart stubborn so I can multiply my miraculous signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
NLT.4: Even then Pharaoh will refuse to listen to you. So I will bring down my fist on Egypt. Then I will rescue my forces — my people, the Israelites — from the land of Egypt with great acts of judgment.
NLT.5: When I raise my powerful hand and bring out the Israelites, the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.”
NLT.6: So Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them.
NLT.7: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three when they made their demands to Pharaoh.
NLT.8: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
NLT.9: “Pharaoh will demand, ‘Show me a miracle.’ When he does this, say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down in front of Pharaoh, and it will become a serpent. ’”
NLT.10: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did what the LORD had commanded them. Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent!
NLT.11: Then Pharaoh called in his own wise men and sorcerers, and these Egyptian magicians did the same thing with their magic.
NLT.12: They threw down their staffs, which also became serpents! But then Aaron’s staff swallowed up their staffs.
NLT.13: Pharaoh’s heart, however, remained hard. He still refused to listen, just as the LORD had predicted.
NLT.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is stubborn, and he still refuses to let the people go.
NLT.15: So go to Pharaoh in the morning as he goes down to the river. Stand on the bank of the Nile and meet him there. Be sure to take along the staff that turned into a snake.
NLT.16: Then announce to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you, “Let my people go, so they can worship me in the wilderness.” Until now, you have refused to listen to him.
NLT.17: So this is what the LORD says: “I will show you that I am the LORD.” Look! I will strike the water of the Nile with this staff in my hand, and the river will turn to blood.
NLT.18: The fish in it will die, and the river will stink. The Egyptians will not be able to drink any water from the Nile.’”
NLT.19: Then the LORD said to Moses: “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and raise your hand over the waters of Egypt — all its rivers, canals, ponds, and all the reservoirs. Turn all the water to blood. Everywhere in Egypt the water will turn to blood, even the water stored in wooden bowls and stone pots.’”
NLT.20: So Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD commanded them. As Pharaoh and all of his officials watched, Aaron raised his staff and struck the water of the Nile. Suddenly, the whole river turned to blood!
NLT.21: The fish in the river died, and the water became so foul that the Egyptians couldn’t drink it. There was blood everywhere throughout the land of Egypt.
NLT.22: But again the magicians of Egypt used their magic, and they, too, turned water into blood. So Pharaoh’s heart remained hard. He refused to listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had predicted.
NLT.23: Pharaoh returned to his palace and put the whole thing out of his mind.
NLT.24: Then all the Egyptians dug along the riverbank to find drinking water, for they couldn’t drink the water from the Nile.
NLT.25: Seven days passed from the time the LORD struck the Nile.
